χάρισμα λέγει– συναχθέντων σὺν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ Χριστοῦ. οἱ φυσιούμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ
πορνεύσαντι διὰ τὴν ἐλλογιμότητα μέρος ἦσαν τοῦ παντός, πάντας δὲ πρὸς τὴν
κατάκρισιν τὴν ἐπὶ τῇ πορνείᾳ συναχθῆναι καλεῖ. 244 Τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ τὴν ψυχήν,
ἀλλὰ τὸ χάρισμα ἔφασαν. 242,ξολ2Ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ παραλόγως κινεῖσθαι καὶ τὴν αἰτίαν
τῆς ὀργῆς 243,ξολ2 ἐπάγει, ὅτι οὐ μόνον πορνεία ἀλλὰ καὶ τοιαύτη ἀκούεται παρ'
ὑμῶν οἵα οὐδὲ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. καὶ μέγα φρονεῖτε ὅτι τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ κόσμου
κεκαλλώπισθε. δέον πενθεῖν ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὅτι πορνείαν οὐδὲ τοῖς ἄλλοις συνήθη
τετόλμηκεν· τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ πένθος ἢ ἐχώριζεν τὸν πορνεύσαντα ἐπιμένοντα τῇ
πορνείᾳ, ἢ αὐτὴν τὴν ἀτοπίαν ἐχώριζεν καὶ αὐτὸν ἐπανήγαγεν τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἵνα τὸ
πνεῦμα σωθῇ. Οὐκ ἀπεργασάμενον εἶπεν ἀλλὰ κατεργασάμενον, κἂν τούτῳ ἵνα
ἐμφήνῃ ὅτι πολλῇ παραμονῇ χρησάμενος εἰργάσατο τὸ κακόν, καὶ οὐ συναρπαγεὶς
ἥμαρτεν ἵνα σχῇ καὶ ἀπολογίαν. καὶ ἱκανὸς μὲν ἦν καὶ μόνος ὁ ἀπόστολος
κατακρῖναι ἐκεῖνον, ἀλλὰ θέλει συμψήφους αὐτῷ γενέσθαι καὶ τοὺς Korινθίους,
ὅπως ἂν οὕτω καταρθεῖεν, χωρισθέντες τῆς τοῦ παρανόμου κοινωνίας, καὶ μάλιστα
οἱ ἐπὶ παιδεύσει πεφυσημένοι. οὐχ ὡς ὑποβάλλων δὲ αὐτὸν τῇ τοῦ σατανᾶ ἐξουσίᾳ
τοῦτο ποιεῖ– ἢ γὰρ ἂν ηὔφρανε τοῦτο ποιῶν τὸν σατανᾶν–ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ τῷ σατανᾷ
εἰώθαμεν ἀνατιθέναι πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸν βίον χαλεπά, οἷον νόσους, λύπας, πένθη,
περιστάσεις ἑτέρας, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς πού φησιν ὁ ἀπόστολος· ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ σατᾶν,
ἵνα με κολαφίζῃ. κατὰ τοῦτον δὴ τὸν τρόπον καὶ νῦν παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν κελεύει τῷ
σατανᾷ, τοῦτ' ἔστι ταῖς τοῦ βίου δυσκολίαις. 244,ξολ2 Ταῖς τοῦ βίου κακώσεσι
παραδίδωσιν· τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκός, οὐκ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ψυχῆς,
ἵνα ἐκ τῶν συμβαινόντων τῷ σώματι διεγερθεὶς μετανοήσῃ καὶ σωθῇ τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ
πνεῦμα ὅπερ ἐστὶ τὸ χάρισμα· οὐ γὰρ ὧδε τὴν ψυχὴν λέγει ὡς τῆς σαρκὸς μὲν οὐκ
ἀνισταμένης, τῆς δὲ ψυχῆς μόνης σωζομένης. 1 Kor 5,6Ὁρᾷς ὅτι ἐκαυχῶντο ἐπ'
ἐκείνῳ, οὐ τῇ ἀτοπίᾳ τοῦ πταίσματος προσέχοντες, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ τῆς ἐλλογιμότητος
αὐτοῦ φυσιούμενοι.Ἐκαυχῶντο γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτῷ, οὐ τῷ πταίσματι αὐτοῦ προσέχοντες
ἀλλὰ τῇ παιδείᾳ φυσώμενοι. Κελεύει αὐτὸν ἐκβληθῆναι, ἵνα μὴ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ
συνόντες αὐτῷ πρὸς τὸ ἁμαρτεῖν ὁρμήσωσιν ἀναιδῶς. 1 Kor 5,7 Παλαιὰν ζύμην τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν καλεῖ, ᾗ ὁ παλαιὸς συνεζυμώθη ἄνθρωπος. Τὸν τύπον μετάγει ἐπὶ τὴν
ἀλήθειαν· τὰ γὰρ παρὰἸουδαίοις ἄζυμα μὴ ἀναπεφυρμένα παλαιᾷ ζύμῃ τοὺς νέους
ἀνθρώπους προεδήλου μὴ πεφυρμένους ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις τοῦ παλαιοῦ ἀνθρώπου.Ὁ
παρὰἸουδαίοις ἀμνὸς θυόμενος τὸ πάθος καὶ πόλον μυστήριον τῆς οἰκονομίας
ἐδήλου τοῦ σταυροῦ. τὰ δὲ ἑξῆς φησιν, ἐπεὶ περιεργαστικώτερον πως ἡ ζύμη,
ἁπλούστερον δὲ τὸ ἄζυμον. 1 Kor 5,8 Τῇ τροπῇ ἐνέμεινεν ὡσανεὶ ἔλεγεν· μὴ ἐν
πονηρῷ βίῳ καὶ κακῷ, ἀλλ' ἐν βίῳ μὴ ἔχοντι ἐπιμιξίαν τῆς παλαιᾶς ἐκείνης ζύμης·
τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας. 245 1 Kor 5,9–10 Οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῃ,
ἀλλ' ἐν ταύτῃ ἔγραψεν. διὰ δὲ τοῦτο οὐ κωλύει τοῖς ἔξωθεν συνεῖναι, ἐπειδὴ εἰ
πάντας ἐξετρέποντο τοὺς τοιούτους, ἐμποδίζεσθαι συνέβαινε τὸ κήρυγμα· τοιοῦτοι
γὰρ πάντες ὡς εἰπεῖν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν οὓς συνέβαινεν ὠφελεῖσθαι ἐκ τῆς συνουσίας
τῶν πιστευσάντων. δηλοῖ οὖν τοῖς μὲν οἰκείοις ἁμαρτάνουσιν ἐπιπλήττειν, τοὺς δὲ
πεπλανημένους παρακαλεῖν. 1 Kor 5,9. 13 Τὸ ἔγραψα οὐχ ἑτέρας ἐστὶν ἐπιστολῆς
ἀλλὰ ταύτης, λέγει γάρ· νῦν δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν. τὸ δὲ ἐξαρεῖτε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν
αὐτῶν, Μωϋσέως ἐστὶ φωνὴ ἣν δευτεροῖ Παῦλος. Μέμνηται ῥήσεως ἐν τῇ παλαιᾷ
κειμένης, δεικνὺς ὅτι οὐ μόνον αὐτοὶ ὠφελοῦνται ὥσπερ λοιμοῦ τινος
ἀπαλλαγέντες, ἀλλ' οὔτε καινοτομία τὸ τοιοῦτον, ἀλλ' ὅτι καὶ τῷ νομοθέτῃ τοῦτο
ἐδόκει, τὸ τοὺς τοιούτους ἐκτέμνεσθαι. 1 Kor 5,12 Εἰκότως τοῦτο εἶπεν· τῶν γὰρ
pass_a_gloss: (Continuing: and by spirit he means the) gift - 'when (you) have been gathered with the power of Christ'. Those puffed up over the one who fornicated because of (his) eloquence were a part of the whole, but he calls all to be gathered for the condemnation over the fornication. [page 244] The spirit, they said, (is) not the soul but the gift. [Second column, pages 242-244, parallel to the 5:1-5 notes:] So that he may not seem to be moved unreasonably, he also adds the cause of the anger: that not only fornication, but such (fornication) is heard among you as (is) not even among the Gentiles. And you think big because you have been beautified with the wisdom of the world, when it is needful to mourn over him because he dared a fornication not customary even to the others. For this mourning would either separate the one who fornicated, persisting in the fornication, or would separate the absurdity itself and bring back the man himself, so that the spirit may be saved. He did not say 'having done' but 'having worked out', even in this to make evident that using much persistence he worked the evil, and did not sin being snatched away so as to have also a defence. And the apostle was sufficient even alone to condemn that man, but he wishes the Corinthians also to become fellow-voters with him, so that thus they might be cleansed (καταρθεῖεν, read καθαρθεῖεν), separated from the fellowship of the lawless one, and especially those puffed up over education. He does not do this as subjecting him to the authority of Satan - for doing this he would have gladdened Satan - but since we are accustomed to attribute to Satan all the hard things in life, such as diseases, griefs, mournings, other circumstances, as also the apostle himself says somewhere: 'a thorn of Satan was given to me, so that he may buffet me' (2 Cor 12:7). In this very manner now too he orders (them) to hand him over to Satan, that is, to the difficulties of life. [page 244, col. 2] He hands (him) over to the afflictions of life; for this is the 'for destruction of the flesh', not for perdition of soul, so that, roused from the things happening to the body, he may repent and the spirit in him, which is the gift, may be saved; for he does not here mean the soul, as though the flesh did not rise and the soul alone were saved. [Label 1 Cor 5:6.] You see that they boasted over that man, not paying attention to the absurdity of the fall, but puffed up by his eloquence. (Unmarked second form:) For they boasted over him, not paying attention to his fall but puffed up by (his) education. He orders him to be cast out, so that the rest too, being with him, may not rush shamelessly toward sinning. [Label 1 Cor 5:7.] He calls sin old leaven, with which the old man was leavened together. He carries the type over to the truth: for the unleavened (loaves) among the Jews, not kneaded with old leaven, foreshowed the new men not mixed with the sins of the old man. The lamb sacrificed among the Jews showed the Passion and the (πόλον, read ὅλον?) whole mystery of the dispensation of the cross. And he says the following (things), since leaven (is) somehow more elaborate, but the unleavened simpler. [Label 1 Cor 5:8.] He remained in the figure, as if he said: not in a wicked and bad life, but in a life having no admixture of that old leaven; for this is 'in unleavened (bread) of sincerity and truth'. [page 245; Label 1 Cor 5:9-10.] Not in another (letter), but in this one he wrote. And for this reason he does not forbid being with those outside, since if they turned away from all such (people), the preaching would happen to be hindered; for all, so to speak, among the Gentiles were such, whom it happened to be benefited from the company of those who had believed. So he shows (that one should) rebuke one's own (people) when sinning, but exhort those who have strayed. [Label 1 Cor 5:9, 13 (second form of the 5:9 note, then 5:13).] 'I wrote' is not of another letter but of this one, for he says: 'but now I have written to you' (1 Cor 5:11). And 'you shall remove the wicked from among yourselves' is a voice of Moses which Paul repeats (Deut 17:7). He mentions a saying lying in the Old (Testament), showing that not only are they benefited, as freed from some plague, but neither is such a thing an innovation, but that this seemed (right) also to the lawgiver, that such (people) be cut off. [Label 1 Cor 5:12.] Reasonably he said this; for of the (… continues in the next section).
pass_b_english: …the gift), "when you are gathered together, with the power of Christ." Those who were puffed up over the fornicator because of his eloquence were only part of the whole church, but he calls everyone to gather to condemn the fornication. By "the spirit," they have said, he means not the soul but the gift.

The second catena form adds: So as not to seem stirred to anger without reason, he adds its cause: not only fornication, but fornication of a kind not found even among the Gentiles, is reported among you. And you are proud of having been adorned with the wisdom of the world, when you ought to mourn over him for daring a fornication that is not customary even among others. He did not say "who did" but "who has carried out," to make plain that he did the evil with long persistence; he did not sin because he was swept away, which would have given him some excuse. The apostle could have condemned him on his own, but he wants the Corinthians to cast their votes with him, so that in this way they may be cleansed by cutting themselves off from fellowship with the lawbreaker, above all those who were puffed up over their learning. He does not do this to put the man under Satan's power, for by doing that he would have delighted Satan. Rather, we are used to blaming Satan for all the hardships of life, such as diseases, griefs, bereavements and other troubles; as the apostle himself says somewhere, "A thorn of Satan was given to me, to buffet me" (2 Corinthians 12:7). In just this way he now orders him handed over to Satan, that is, to the hardships of life. He hands him over to life's afflictions, for that is what "for the destruction of the flesh" means, not the ruin of the soul: so that, roused by what happens to his body, he may repent, and the spirit in him, which is the gift, may be saved. He does not mean the soul here, as though the flesh did not rise and the soul alone were saved.

On 1 Corinthians 5:6: You see that they boasted about him. They paid no attention to how shocking his fall was; his eloquence had puffed them up. He orders him expelled, so that the rest, by keeping company with him, do not also rush shamelessly into sin.

On 1 Corinthians 5:7: By "old leaven" he means sin, with which the old man was leavened through and through. He carries the type over to the reality. The unleavened bread of the Jews, unmixed with old leaven, foreshadowed the new people, unmixed with the sins of the old man. The lamb sacrificed among the Jews showed forth the Passion and the [whole] mystery of the dispensation of the cross. He says what follows because leaven is a more elaborate thing, while unleavened bread is simpler.

On 1 Corinthians 5:8: He stayed with the figure, as if to say: not in a wicked and evil life, but in a life with no admixture of that old leaven. That is what "with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth" means.

On 1 Corinthians 5:9–10: He wrote this not in another letter but in this one. He does not forbid keeping company with outsiders, because if they had shunned everyone of that kind, the preaching would have been hindered. Nearly everyone among the Gentiles, so to speak, was like that, and these people stood to gain from the company of believers. So he makes clear that we should rebuke our own people when they sin, but appeal to those who have gone astray.
The second catena form adds: He says, after all, "But now I have written to you" (1 Corinthians 5:11).

On 1 Corinthians 5:13: "Drive out the wicked man from among yourselves" is a saying of Moses which Paul repeats (Deuteronomy 17:7). He recalls a saying found in the Old Testament to show not only that they gain by it, like people rid of a plague, but also that such a step is no innovation: the lawgiver too thought that such people should be cut off.
On 1 Corinthians 5:12: He said this with good reason, for it is of his own…

lemmas.gloss: voting with, of the same vote

choices.english: printed after 'The second catena form adds:' except one sentence
choices.why: Second-column run on 5:1-5. Only the mourning sentence ('this mourning would either separate ...') repeats the first form in u02-rem-close and is not reprinted; the rest (cause of anger, long persistence, Corinthians' vote, Satan as life's hardships, 'destruction of the flesh') has no counterpart.
rejected: printing it as main text (old English)

choices.term: Ἐκαυχῶντο γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτῷ ... τῇ παιδείᾳ φυσώμενοι (5:6)
choices.why: Unmarked second form of the 5:6 note; same claim with παιδεία for ἐλλογιμότης (SOURCE_ISSUES item 5).

choices.english: first sentence collapsed into the 5:9-10 note; its proof text printed after 'The second catena form adds:'; the 5:13 remark labelled 'On 1 Corinthians 5:13:'
choices.why: 'Τὸ ἔγραψα οὐχ ἑτέρας ἐστὶν ἐπιστολῆς ἀλλὰ ταύτης' repeats 'Οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῃ, ἀλλ' ἐν ταύτῃ ἔγραψεν' (item 5); the rest of that note is on 5:13, so it is labelled by the words of its lemma.
πόλον is corrupt; ὅλον fits the sense. The guess is bracketed and noted.
rejected: the passion and the cross as a mystery (old English)

choices.why: SOURCE_ISSUES item 16: the old English used 'Regarding 1 Corinthians 5:6, you see' and 'In 1 Corinthians 5:7, he calls'; one form now.
